member.name: NamedMarkLedger
member.para: Why this class exists at all: Scan was blind to named marks, and nobody had ever written down why. Until 2026-08-30 a prologue, an epilogue or a --custom mark could only ever be found by Probe. carried no reference to whatsoever, and the question "was that deliberate?" was asked and could not be answered: the file's doc comments said nothing, there was no notes file for it, the CHANGELOG and the manual said nothing, no TODO item mentioned it, and none of the eight commits that had touched the file was about named marks. The memory file named-marks-have-no-safety-net recorded the mechanism - every recovery path is triggered by a discontinuity in the chapter numbering, and a named mark carries no number, so it sits in no gap and nothing looks for it twice - and recorded the consequence as a hazard to work around when weighing changes to primary-scan window geometry. It never argued that the exclusion was correct. The blindness had fallen out of gaps being defined by numbers; it had not been decided.

The argument that would have justified it does not cover the tail. The project had reasoned carefully about what can be announced in a given stretch, in 's remarks: between two consecutively numbered chapters no numbered chapter fits, the prologue's scope has closed and the epilogue's has not opened, so only a --custom mapping could be there - and the jingle-first gate handles exactly that case. That reasoning covers an interior gap. It fails for the trailing region, because the epilogue's scope opens precisely there. says so in as many words, about why "between-chapters" is not offered as a keyword for : "that scope does not exclude the tail - it is exactly how the built-in epilogue uses it".

The measurement, 2026-08-30. Over all 179 .debug.log files then available - the 19 of the build-435 corpus run in L:\Temp plus the 160 of the Perry Rhodan Silber-Edition library - 13 of the 14 books that have an epilogue at all have it inside the trailing region: Kampf gegen die Blues, Die letzte Bastion, OLD MAN, Ovaron, Finale für Pluto, Das Tabora, Die Altmutanten, Das Erbe der Yulocs, Suche nach der Erde, Die Terra-Patrouille, Corsa nello spazio, I Shall Wear Midnight and The Forever War - the last of these clearing the region boundary by 2.5 s. The fourteenth is Raumschiff Erde, whose epilogue announcement sits mid-book and is dropped at result-build time by ; it is the "not a hypothetical" case mentions. So the trailing scan re-reads, with the upgrade model, the one stretch where an epilogue belongs - and could not see one.

What this change does not fix, stated plainly. The only recorded loss of a named mark is Gruelfin's Prolog at build 280, and that is a prologue in the head of the file. Scan reaches the head only when an expected start chapter is known, which comes either from --expected-start-chapter or from a prologue having already been found - so the one failure on record has a catch-22 of its own and is untouched by this. The case for the change rests on the structural argument and the 13-of-14 measurement, not on a book anyone can point at where a named mark was lost and this would have caught it. That is the "no known-bad cases" situation the memory evaluating-a-flag-without-known-bad-cases describes, and it is why the change was built to add marks only where Probe found none rather than to second-guess Probe anywhere.

One deliberate behaviour change came with the move. The once-per-phrase out-of-scope note used to live in a RegionProber field, so it was per region rather than per file, and its own doc comment admitted "a recovery pass over a gap may repeat it once". Moving the set onto this per-file ledger makes the note genuinely once per phrase per file, which is what it always claimed to be. Log-only; no mark moves because of it.
